Bachelor of Engineering (Civil Engineering) - Structural Engineering Option

1st & 2nd Semester

1st SEMESTER

Common to Aerospace, Biomedical, Chemical, Civil, Computer, Electrical, Industrial and Mechanical Engineering Programs.

REQUIRED:
Introduction to Engineering
* Writing Skills
General Chemistry
Calculus I
Linear Algebra
Physics: Mechanics

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from Table A .

* Graded on a pass-fail basis.

2nd SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Digital Computation and Programming
Graphics
Principles of Engineering Economics
Calculus II
Materials Science Fundamentals
Physics: Waves and Fields

3rd & 4th Semester

Common to both the Civil Engineering and Structural Engineering Options.

3rd SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Environmental Science and Impact Assessment
Strength of Materials I
Fundamentals of Surveying
Geology for Engineers
Differential Equations and Vector Calculus

Note: All required core courses in 1st and 2nd semester are prerequisites to all required core courses in 3rd semester.

4th SEMESTER

Communication in the Engineering Professions
Transportation Engineering
Hydrology and Water Resources
Probability and Statistics for Engineers
Strength of Materials II
Geotechnical Properties of Soils

5th & 6th Semester

Revised Curriculum Begins 2016-2017.

5th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Structural Analysis
Introduction to Structural Design
Concrete Materials
Foundation Engineering
Numerical Analysis

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from Table A .

6th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Computer Aided Structural Analysis
Structural Concrete Design I
Structural Steel Design
Civil Engineering Systems
Highway Materials

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from Table B .

NOTE: Students who have a CLEAR Academic Standing may opt to enroll in the Industrial Internship Program (IIP). Eligible students should select WKT 90A/B on the course intention form - Please contact the Department of Civil Engineering.

7th & 8th Semester

Revised Curriculum begins 2017-2018.

7th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
CVL 70A/B * Structural Capstone Design Project
Structural Concrete Design II
Bridge Design and Construction
Structural Building Systems

LIBERAL STUDIES: One course from the following:
Science Fiction
Technology and the Contemporary Environment
Scientific Technology and Modern Society
Religion, Science and Philosophy
Power, Change and Technology

8th SEMESTER

REQUIRED:
Law and Ethics in Engineering Practice
CVL 70A/B * Structural Capstone Design Project
Project Management
Pavement Design and Management
Renovation/Repair of Existing Structures

* CVL 70A/B is a two-term course. Students must continue the same project they started in the Fall. Contact the department for more details.
